content: 1. Ketoconazole should be administered at a dose of 6 mg/kg/day orally. In cases of renal impairment, no dosage adjustments are specified in the manufacturer’s labeling. However, ketoconazole tablets should not be used as a first-line treatment. They are only recommended when other effective antifungal therapies are unavailable or not tolerated, and when the potential benefits outweigh the risk of hepatotoxicity. 2. Ketoconazole tablets should not be prescribed for the treatment of skin or nail fungal infections due to the risk of severe liver damage, adrenal gland dysfunction, and harmful drug interactions. These risks outweigh the benefits for these conditions, which are not approved indications for the drug. The FDA removed these indications from the labeling in 2013. 3. Ketoconazole is not recommended for the treatment of fungal meningitis due to its poor penetration into the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). 4. Ketoconazole increases the levels of alfuzosin by inhibiting its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 5. Ketoconazole increases the levels of alprazolam by inhibiting its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 6. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of conivaptan by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration of conivaptan with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, including ketoconazole, is contraindicated. 7. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of dihydroergotamine (both oral and intranasal forms) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 8. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of disopyramide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both disopyramide and ketoconazole prolong the QTc interval, making this combination contraindicated. 9. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of dronedarone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both dronedarone and ketoconazole prolong the QTc interval, making this combination contraindicated. 10. Ketoconazole increases the levels of eliglustat by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors are contraindicated in poor or intermediate metabolizers of eliglustat. In extensive metabolizers, the eliglustat dose should be reduced from 84 mg twice daily to 84 mg once daily when co-administered with strong or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors. Eliglustat is contraindicated if strong or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors are used concomitantly with strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 11. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ergoloid mesylates, ergonovine, and ergotamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. These combinations are contraindicated. 12. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of finerenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 13. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration of flibanserin with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated due to the risk of severe hypotension or syncope. 14. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of gepirone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 15. Both ibutilide and ketoconazole prolong the QTc interval, making their combination contraindicated. 16. Both indapamide and ketoconazole prolong the QTc interval, making their combination contraindicated. 17. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 18. Isoniazid decreases the levels of ketoconazole through an unspecified interaction mechanism. This combination is contraindicated. 19. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ivabradine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration of ivabradine with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 20. Ketoconazole increases the levels of lomitapide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, leading to a several-fold increase in lomitapide levels. This combination is contraindicated. 21. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lonafarnib is a sensitive CYP3A4 substrate, and co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 22. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of lovastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase systemic statin exposure and the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. This combination is contraindicated. 23. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of lurasidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration of lurasidone with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 24. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of mavacamten by inhibiting both CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP2C19 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to mavacamten, potentially leading to heart failure due to systolic dysfunction. This combination is contraindicated. 25. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of methadone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both methadone and ketoconazole prolong the QTc interval, making this combination contraindicated. 26. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of methylergonovine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 27. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of naloxegol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors can significantly increase naloxegol systemic exposure, potentially precipitating opioid withdrawal symptoms. This combination is contraindicated. 28. Ketoconazole decreases the levels or effects of nisoldipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 29. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of pacritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 30. Both pentamidine and ketoconazole prolong the QTc interval, making their combination contraindicated. 31. Both pimozide and ketoconazole prolong the QTc interval. Ketoconazole also increases pimozide levels by inhibiting its metabolism, increasing the risk of QT interval prolongation. This combination is contraindicated. 32. Both procainamide and ketoconazole prolong the QTc interval, making their combination contraindicated. 33. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of quinidine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both quinidine and ketoconazole prolong the QTc interval, making this combination contraindicated. 34. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ranolazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both ranolazine and ketoconazole prolong the QTc interval, making this combination contraindicated. 35. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of silodosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 36. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of simvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the increased risk of rhabdomyolysis. 37. Ketoconazole increases the levels of sirolimus by inhibiting its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 38. Both sotalol and ketoconazole prolong the QTc interval, making their combination contraindicated. 39. Ketoconazole increases the levels of triazolam by inhibiting its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 40. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ulipristal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 41. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of venetoclax by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated during the initial ramp-up dosing phase of venetoclax. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used after the ramp-up phase, the venetoclax dose should be reduced by at least 75%. 42. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of voclosporin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 43. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of abemaciclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used, as ketoconazole can increase abemaciclib AUC by up to 16-fold. 44. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of abrocitinib by inhibiting CYP2C9 and CYP2C19 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used, as it may increase systemic exposure to abrocitinib and its active metabolites, leading to increased adverse effects. 45. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of acalabrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors should be avoided. If a strong CYP3A inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., up to 7 days), temporarily interrupt acalabrutinib treatment. 46. Ketoconazole increases the levels of ado-trastuzumab emtansine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase DM1 (the cytotoxic component of ado-trastuzumab) exposure and toxicity. Consider an alternative drug with minimal CYP3A4 inhibition potential. If unavoidable, delay ado-trastuzumab until the strong CYP3A4 inhibitors have cleared (approximately 3 elimination half-lives of the inhibitors). If ado-trastuzumab cannot be delayed, closely monitor the patient for adverse reactions. 47. Ketoconazole increases the levels of afatinib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This combination should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. If co-administered, reduce the afatinib daily dose by 10 mg if not tolerated. 48. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of almotriptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 49. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of alpelisib by inhibiting BCRP (breast cancer resistance protein). This combination should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. If unavoidable, closely monitor for increased adverse reactions. 50. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of ketoconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. This combination should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 51. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of amiodarone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both amiodarone and ketoconazole prolong the QTc interval, making this combination contraindicated. 52. Both amitriptyline and ketoconazole prolong the QTc interval, making their combination contraindicated. 53. Both amoxapine and ketoconazole prolong the QTc interval, making their combination contraindicated. 54. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of ketoconazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used, as apalutamide is a strong CYP3A4 inducer. 55. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of apixaban by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. Co-administration with strong dual inhibitors of CYP3A4 and P-gp is contraindicated. 56. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of aprepitant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 57. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of avanafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated due to the risk of severe adverse events, including hypotension, syncope, visual changes, and priapism. 58. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of avapritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 59. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of axitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the axitinib dose by 50%. After discontinuation of the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, adjust the axitinib dose to the pre-inhibitor level after 3-5 half-lives of the inhibitor. 60. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 61. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of bedaquiline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors for more than 14 consecutive days should be avoided unless the benefit outweighs the risk. 62. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of belinostat by inhibiting UGT metabolism. This combination should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. If co-administered, reduce the belinostat starting dose to 750 mg/m² in patients who are homozygous for the UGT1A128 allele or when co-administered with UGT inhibitors. 63. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of bosutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This combination should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 64. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of brigatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with a strong CYP3A inhibitor cannot be avoided, reduce the brigatinib dose by approximately 50%. After discontinuation of the strong CYP3A inhibitor, resume the brigatinib dose that was tolerated prior to initiating the inhibitor. 65. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of bromocriptine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 66. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used.
